elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: The minimum monthly fee survives: "a minimum monthly fee (\"Monthly Base Fee\") for certain bundled data processing Services" and "All minimum monthly fees (including the Monthly Base Fee) are due in advance on the first day of the calendar month". New Section 8.1A expressly preserves a "minimum monthly fee commitment" rather than eliminating it.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Customer must pay the committed minimum even where actual usage is lower: "If Customer's actual usage-based charges for such period are less than the committed amount, Customer shall pay the difference as a true-up", plus advance ACH debit of minimum monthly fees. Payment is therefore not limited to usage or ordered Services.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Section 8.1A: "Customer's minimum monthly fee commitment (including the Monthly Base Fee) is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term". This caps the eight-year minimum (Term running to "the eighth anniversary of the Commencement Date") at a rolling 12-month window.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.1A: "Customer may reduce such commitment upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to M&I", and the retained sourcing obligation in 10.3.A is expressly qualified: "during the Term, and subject to Customer's reduction right in Section 8.1A", so no retained sentence contradicts the new right.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Section 8.1A: "Customer shall pay the difference as a true-up, and no penalty or shortfall charge shall apply." The mechanic is a payment of the differential only, with penalty/shortfall charges expressly excluded.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the single inserted Section 8.1A supplies all three atomic elements (12-month cap, 30 days' notice reduction right, true-up with express no-penalty language) in operative text, not merely in the comment.
Preferred level correctly fails: the Monthly Base Fee minimum and its advance-payment/ACH-debit machinery are retained, so Customer still pays irrespective of usage.

Minimality holds. The insertion is a concise new clause for a commitment that had no exit, and the only other edit ('and subject to Customer's reduction right in Section 8.1A' in 10.3.A) is necessary to stop the retained mandatory-sourcing sentence from contradicting the new reduction right; the 'during the Term' sourcing period, the advance-payment mechanics, the collection-fee language and the ERV formula are all left intact, and nothing outside the checklist is deleted or added.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles. The ERV formula still operates on 'the greater of (a) the Monthly Base Fee ... and (b) the average monthly Fees', which remains computable after a reduction.

Residual exposure to note in the cover comment (not an element failure here): ERV still multiplies the Monthly Base Fee by all months remaining to the eighth anniversary, so on early termination M&I can recover the pre-reduction minimum economics. That is properly a termination-fee/liquidated-damages issue, but consider adding words tying ERV to the commitment as reduced under Section 8.1A if the termination rule does not already address it, otherwise M&I may argue the 12-month cap is defeated on exit.

Optional tightening: Section 8.1A does not state a floor or maximum extent of reduction ('may reduce such commitment' is open-ended in Customer's favour) and does not say whether the reduction takes effect for the balance of the then-current 12-month period. This does not defeat the fallback element as written, but expect Vendor to push for a floor; be ready to fix the effective date of the reduction rather than the quantum.
